articles.title: Texas County Treasurer Challenges Law Requiring Her To Lose Salary Because She Ran on Abolishing Her Office
articles.summary: Adriane Hodges was elected treasurer of Bell County on a platform of abolishing the office. She says a state law requiring her to forego a salary because of...
articles.body:
A recently elected Texas county treasurer who ran on abolishing her office has filed a First Amendment lawsuit after the county slashed her budget to $0 because of her campaign platform.

After Adriane Hodges was elected treasurer of Bell County earlier this month, county officials set her budgeted salary for the upcoming year to $0, citing a section of the Texas Local Government Code that requires county officers who publicly advocated for the abolition of their office to file an affidavit electing not to be paid. Hodges hasn't signed that affidavit yet, nor does she believe that she should be forced to.

The Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression (FIRE), a free speech advocacy group, filed a federal civil rights lawsuit against Bell County on Hodges' behalf on Thursday. The lawsuit argues that "imposing consequences for expressing a particular opinion is textbook viewpoint discrimination" under the First Amendment. Hodges' suit additionally argues that requiring her to sign an affidavit stating she does not want to receive a salary, which is untrue, is unconstitutional compelled speech.

"I ran on a promise to shrink the county government," Hodges said in a FIRE press release . "I believe that eliminating the county treasurer's office will save taxpayer money. That's what I told the voters, and that's what they elected me to do. Rather than accept that, the county punished me for my speech. The ones who are really being punished are the voters who chose my vision for how their government should work for them."

Hodges campaigned on rolling the county treasurer's office into the office of the county auditor, a move that 11 other Texas counties have made. The most recent example is Galveston County, which shut down its county treasurer's office in 2023, one year after electing Hank Dugie on an explicit abolition platform.

"I'm asking voters to hire me so I can fire myself," Hodges said when she announced her candidacy.

One could argue that if a politician believes their office shouldn't exist, they should put their money where their mouth is, but in practice, such a policy would discourage those who believe in shrinking government from running for office or expressing their beliefs, while favoring pro-government candidates. FIRE argues that this violates a core First Amendment principle of viewpoint neutrality when it comes to government policies.

"One perverse consequence of Texas' law is that it actually punishes candidates for being honest with voters," Heather Pincus, a FIRE staff attorney, said in the press release. "If Adriane had lied or hidden her plans to eliminate the treasurer's office, she would be able to draw a public salary while implementing that policy. It's only because she expressed her opinion that it should be eliminated that she will be stripped of her pay."

Hodges' lawsuit aims to strike down the Texas political speech code completely. It seeks permanent and preliminary injunctions declaring the code unconstitutional on its face and as-applied to Hodges, as well as damages and attorney fees.

Candidates running kamikaze campaigns against local governments is a long and amusing tradition in American history. Many notorious speed-trap towns were shut down by their own disgusted residents. Take the case of St. George, Missouri, where in 2011, a local alderman with the campaign slogan "Save Us From Our City" ousted the incumbent mayor. St. George voted in favor of dissolution later that year.

articles.title: Jair Bolsonaro: Defesa pede a Moraes visitas diárias de filhos | G1
articles.standfirst: Ex-presidente deu entrada em hospital de Brasília nesta sexta (20) após sentir dores abdominais. Solicitação feita ao STF contempla Carlos, Jair Renan e filha menor de idade.
articles.summary: Jair Bolsonaro está internado em Brasília com obstrução intestinal e sua defesa pede ao ministro Alexandre de Moraes que os filhos possam visitá-lo diariamente.
articles.body:
A defesa de Jair Bolsonaro pediu neste sábado (21) ao ministro Alexandre de Moraes , do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), autorização para que três de seus filhos — Carlos, Jair Renan e a filha menor de idade — possam visitar o ex-presidente diariamente enquanto durar sua internação no Hospital DF Star, em Brasília .

Bolsonaro deu entrada no hospital particular na tarde desta sexta-feira (20) após apresentar um quadro de dor e distensão abdominal .

"Diante da nova circunstância e considerando o período de internação hospitalar, requer, em caráter de urgência, seja autorizado o ingresso de seus filhos Carlos Nantes Bolsonaro e Jair Renan Bolsonaro, bem como [de sua filha], para que possam visitá-lo diariamente, enquanto perdurar a internação", afirma a defesa no pedido enviado a Moraes.

🔎Bolsonaro tem outros dois filhos: o ex-deputado Eduardo Bolsonaro , que deixou o Brasil em 2025, e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), que fugiu do país após a derrota na eleição presidencial de outubro deste ano . Ambos estão nos Estados Unidos.

Nesta sexta, o ex-presidente deixou sua residência em Brasília , onde cumpre prisão domiciliar humanitária desde março deste ano, sob escolta da Polícia Militar do Distrito Federal, após avaliação do cardiologista Brasil Caiado.

De acordo com a equipe médica, exames feitos no hospital identificaram uma obstrução parcial no intestino delgado associada a aderências na parede abdominal , sequelas das cirurgias realizadas desde a facada sofrida em setembro de 2018.

Segundo boletim médico e informações do médico Brasil Caiado desta sexta-feira ( veja no vídeo acima ), o ex-presidente está estável, consciente e recebendo medicação . Uma nova cirurgia não está descartada.

Em uma rede social, o filho Carlos Bolsonaro , senador eleito pelo PL de Santa Catarina, comentou neste sábado o estado de saúde do pai, afirmando que os médicos colocaram uma sonda nasal no ex-presidente para retirada de resíduos alimentares. Ele também disse que Jair Bolsonaro estava com dores e enjoos.

Ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro em 29/9/2025 — Foto: Reuters/Diego Herculano

Condenado a 27 anos e 3 meses de prisão por tentativa de golpe , Bolsonaro iniciou o cumprimento da pena em novembro de 2025 e passou por sucessivas internações ao longo do último ano.

Em dezembro de 2025, foi submetido a uma cirurgia de hérnia inguinal bilateral; em janeiro de 2026, sofreu uma queda e um traumatismo cranioencefálico leve enquanto estava detido na Superintendência da Polícia Federal.

Em março de 2026, após ser internado com suspeita de broncopneumonia quando estava na Papudinha, obteve de Alexandre de Moraes o benefício da prisão domiciliar humanitária, posteriormente prorrogado a pedido dos advogados em razão do quadro clínico.

articles.title: Paixão pela pesca atravessa gerações e jovem vê atividade como apoio | G1
articles.standfirst: Neste Dia Mundial da Pesca, Luiz Henrique Szeremeta, morador de Floresta do Sul, distrito de Presidente Prudente (SP), aprendeu a pescar ainda criança, acompanhando os pais e os avós.
articles.summary: Luiz Henrique Ferreira Szeremeta, de 18 anos, de Presidente Prudente (SP), utiliza a pesca como aliada de sua saúde mental. O hábito alivia a rotina.
articles.body:
Neste Dia Mundial da Pesca, um jovem da região de Presidente Prudente (SP) que frequenta os rios desde antes dos 3 anos de idade destaca os benefícios da pescaria para o convívio familiar , para a socialização das pessoas e para a prevenção aos vícios.

O gosto pela pesca começou cedo na vida de Luiz Henrique Ferreira Szeremeta, que acompanhava os pais nas pescarias em córregos onde a família se reunia em fins de semana. Hoje, aos 18 anos, o jovem natural de Floresta do Sul, distrito de Presidente Prudente (SP), mantém viva essa tradição familiar, alimentada por histórias contadas pelos pais e avós.

O que começou como um passeio de criança, em meio a varas e molinetes, se transformou em parte da rotina e hoje é uma oportunidade de estar em contato com a natureza, encontrar amigos e familiares e aliviar o peso das preocupações cotidianas.

"Hoje com 18 anos, minha relação com a pesca já deixou de ser somente um lazer e se tornou parte do meu dia a dia também, preparando iscas, limpando equipamentos e até mesmo indo pescar quando eu estou tranquilo", disse Luiz Henrique.

A paixão foi construída aos poucos. Primeiro, com os passeios em família; depois, com a curiosidade de aprender mais sobre os equipamentos e as técnicas. Luiz Henrique passou da vara de bambu para o molinete e, mais tarde, para a carretilha.

Também buscou conhecimento em vídeos na internet e passou a se interessar pela pesca esportiva, especialmente com iscas artificiais para capturar traíras e tucunarés .

Paixão pela pesca atravessa gerações e jovem do interior de SP vê atividade como aliada da saúde mental — Foto: Luiz Henrique Ferreira/Arquivo Pessoal

Para Luiz Henrique, a pesca também é uma forma de manter os laços familiares. Ele conta que os pais e os avós sempre gostaram da atividade e que as histórias compartilhadas por eles foram importantes para despertar sua paixão.

O pai, José Ronaldo Szeremeta, lembra que os passeios de pesca fazem parte da história da família desde que o filho era pequeno. Mais do que a captura dos peixes, ele destaca a diversão e o aprendizado proporcionados pelos momentos juntos.

“Eu aprendi que a pesca pode ir muito além de um hobby, pode divertir uma pessoa que passa a semana inteira trabalhando, Pode mostrar a natureza para quem sempre viveu na cidade, pode abrir horizontes na imaginação de uma criança e sempre tendo aquela resenha com os amigos e familiares mesmo sem pegar peixe algum”, afirmou.

Atualmente, Luiz Henrique costuma pescar com amigos e familiares em pesqueiros, rios e córregos. Para ele, cada saída proporciona experiências que não dependem necessariamente de conseguir fisgar um peixe.

Além de uma tradição familiar, Luiz Henrique vê na pesca uma maneira de se afastar das preocupações da rotina. Entre o trabalho como auxiliar administrativo e os estudos de Educação Física, ele encontra na atividade um momento descarregar a mente.

O jovem ainda acredita que o contato com a natureza, a concentração exigida pela pescaria e a convivência com outras pessoas ajudam a aliviar o estresse e a ansiedade.

Na avaliação dele, a atividade também pode ser uma alternativa de lazer para jovens, contribuindo para afastá-los de drogas e outros vícios.

"A pesca pode afastar pessoas de drogas e vícios, controla a ansiedade e ajuda a ter mais foco no dia a dia. Aos pais: incentivem seus filhos a praticar a pesca ou qualquer outro esporte. Aos filhos: mostrem aos seus pais uma opção de diversão para tirar o peso do dia a dia das costas", declara, ao g1 .

articles.title: Saída de Jensen Huang da Nvidia pode frear a onda da IA? | G1
articles.standfirst: O ex-CEO da fabricante de chips é uma das figuras centrais da expansão da inteligência artificial.
articles.summary: O ex-CEO da fabricante de chips é uma das figuras centrais da expansão da inteligência artificial.
articles.body:
Jensen Huang renunciou ao cargo em 12 de novembro. — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

A Nvidia e seu cofundador, Jensen Huang, estão no centro da onda de investimentos em inteligência artificial (IA).

Poucas empresas ou executivos tiveram tanta influência sobre o desenvolvimento da IA nos últimos anos. Sob o comando de Huang , a fabricante americana de chips se tornou essencial para o avanço dessa tecnologia que está transformando o mundo.

Essa parceria chegou ao fim com a renúncia de Huang na semana passada, após a revelação de casos extraconjugais, um deles supostamente com uma espiã chinesa .

O escândalo abalou a Nvidia , que perdeu centenas de bilhões de dólares em valor de mercado. A saída de Huang também gerou dúvidas sobre as consequências de sua ausência para os negócios da empresa.

Embora seja menos conhecida do público do que outras gigantes de tecnologia, como Apple , Amazon e Microsoft , a Nvidia também teve um papel importante na forte valorização das ações nos EUA nos últimos anos.

Os bilhões de dólares investidos em IA e na construção de centros de dados impulsionaram a economia americana, e a Nvidia está entre as empresas que mais investem no setor.

No início, a empresa fabricava chips para processar gráficos de jogos de computador. Depois, passou a desenvolver chips para sistemas de IA e hoje domina esse mercado.

A Nvidia está entre as empresas mais valiosas, avaliada em US$ 3,8 trilhões (cerca de R$ 22 trilhões, considerando a cotação atual) . Na terça-feira (17/11), a companhia afirmou que seu crescimento acelerado deverá continuar, depois de registrar vendas trimestrais duas vezes maiores do que no mesmo período do ano anterior.

Mas agora há incertezas sobre os rumos da empresa. Huang teve um papel fundamental na empresa, liderando sua entrada no mercado de IA, e exercia um controle rigoroso sobre as operações. Até 200 funcionários respondiam diretamente a ele.

Dan Coatsworth, diretor de mercados da empresa de investimentos AJ Bell, afirma que Huang também desempenhava um papel importante na divulgação dos avanços da IA , ajudando a despertar interesse e atrair investimentos para o setor.

Por isso, segundo Coatsworth, sua saída representa um "risco real" de a Nvidia mudar de estratégia e reduzir os investimentos.

Essa decisão poderia desacelerar os investimentos em IA em todo o setor, com consequências para a economia. Mas qual seria o tamanho desse impacto? Segundo Coatsworth, ainda é "incerto".

"Se eles decidirem adotar uma postura muito mais cautelosa... isso poderá provocar um efeito em cadeia, fazendo com que várias empresas de infraestrutura de IA percam repentinamente uma importante fonte de financiamento", afirma Coatsworth.

Kunjan Sobhani, analista do setor de tecnologia da Bloomberg Intelligence, espera que o impacto da saída de Huang seja "limitado" por enquanto, já que a Nvidia tem compromissos comerciais firmados e uma grande carteira de pedidos. Mas, segundo Sobhani, esse cenário poderá mudar no longo prazo.

Ao se tornar líder da indústria de IA, a Nvidia criou uma complexa rede de acordos por meio de uma prática conhecida como "financiamento circular".

A empresa não apenas vende chips a clientes como Meta, SpaceX e OpenAI , mas também financia essas companhias e outras que integram sua cadeia de fornecedores, seja concedendo empréstimos, seja investindo diretamente nelas.

Esse modelo preocupa alguns investidores, que temem as consequências de uma possível redução do financiamento oferecido pela Nvidia . Sem esses recursos, outras empresas do setor poderiam cortar gastos ou demitir funcionários? E esses efeitos poderiam atingir o restante da economia dos EUA?

Esse risco talvez explique por que executivos do setor de tecnologia, como Elon Musk e Tim Sweeney, presidente-executivo da Epic Games, empresa responsável pelo jogo Fortnite, pediram que Huang volte ao comando da Nvidia .

Musk afirmou que "acordos fundamentais" envolvendo a tecnologia da Nvidia seriam perdidos após a saída de Huang. A renúncia dele também levou acionistas e apoiadores a lançar uma campanha chamada Bring Jensen Back ("Tragam Jensen de Volta", em tradução livre).

O próprio Huang afirmou que está disposto a voltar à empresa, poucos dias depois de renunciar.

Coatsworth afirma nunca ter visto o financiamento circular ser usado em uma escala tão grande, mas reconhece que a existência de empresas concorrentes poderia proteger o restante da indústria de IA de uma eventual desaceleração da Nvidia .

Após as revelações sobre os relacionamentos de Huang, as ações da Nvidia despencaram. Em contrapartida, as de fabricantes de semicondutores concorrentes, como AMD, Broadcom e Marvell Technology, dispararam.

"Não acho que toda a atividade de IA vá parar se a Nvidia desacelerar e reduzir parte do financiamento, mas isso muda a maneira como as pessoas enxergam toda a situação", acrescenta Coatsworth.

A possibilidade de desaceleração já provocou turbulências nos mercados de ações. Os avanços do Partido Democrata nas eleições legislativas de meio de mandato nos EUA preocuparam investidores, já que muitos candidatos do partido defenderam regras mais rígidas para as empresas de IA durante a campanha.

Também há dúvidas sobre se os enormes investimentos em IA realmente trarão retorno financeiro.

Segundo o banco de investimentos Goldman Sachs, os investimentos em IA devem ultrapassar US$ 1 trilhão (cerca de R$ 5,8 trilhões, considerando a cotação atual) em 2026. O banco afirmou que a tecnologia continuará sendo o "principal motor do crescimento dos investimentos empresariais" no próximo ano.

Colette Kress, que assume o comando da Nvidia por enquanto, afirmou que a empresa continua "funcionando normalmente" sem Huang na liderança e que seu rápido crescimento segue conforme o previsto.

A alta das ações das gigantes de tecnologia tem ajudado a proteger a economia americana de crises e outros impactos econômicos internacionais, incluindo os efeitos das tarifas comerciais. Essa valorização também beneficia investimentos e fundos de aposentadoria de pessoas em todo o mundo.

Embora Huang tenha afirmado que seria "uma honra" voltar ao comando da Nvidia , o conselho de administração declarou que não considera sua reintegração.

E, embora Coatsworth acredite que "nenhum CEO é insubstituível", ele reconhece que quem assumir o lugar de Huang enfrentará uma grande pressão.

articles.title: Trump formally ends minting of the penny after nearly 250 years of production
articles.summary: The U.S. Mint, which began producing the currency in 1793, has said it costs nearly 4 cents to make each penny.
articles.body: Washington is officially done with spending a pretty penny on penny production. President Donald Trump on Friday signed the bipartisan Common Cents Act, which formally directs the federal government to stop minting the penny. Both the House and the Senate passed the measure by voice vote, meaning no notable opposition. “It costs nearly FOUR cents to make just one penny,” the bill’s author, Rep. Lisa McClain, R-Mich., said Sept. 29 on X a day after Senate passage. “This legislation will save $85 million per year by permanently ending penny production — it’s common sense!” The U.S. Mint last year put the immediate annual savings of discontinuing penny production at $56 million. The government stopped making pennies in November 2025, nine months after Trump called for the Treasury Department to stop production, writing at the time that the process was “so wasteful!” However, the U.S. Mint said it would still produce collector versions to be produced in “limited quantities.” The penny can still be used as legal tender “for all debts, public charges, taxes, and dues,” according to the new law. The Treasury Department said last year that the Federal Reserve will continue to recirculate the approximately 114 billion pennies that are in existence “for as long as possible.” The new measure also provides a procedure for stores and businesses that accept cash payments to round their prices to the nearest amount divisible by 5 cents. And, as the nickel replaces the penny at the bottom of the U.S. Mint’s currency list, that coin can now be manufactured with an inner layer of zinc and an outer layer of nickel. It is currently produced with nickel and copper, which costs more than zinc. Congress passed the Coinage Act in 1792, and the U.S. Mint began producing the penny, known officially as the cent, the following year. In its nearly 250 years in production, the penny has had multiple facades. It wasn’t until 1909 that it was given its modern-day face, featuring President Abraham Lincoln. The first penny, produced in 1787, had a sundial design created by Benjamin Franklin. After the U.S. Mint took over, the penny was slightly bigger and included the image of a woman representing Liberty on one side and 15 chain links on the other. The next penny debuted in 1857, taking on a smaller shape and displaying a flying eagle design on one side and a wreath on the other. It also changed from being 100% copper to 88% copper and 12% nickel. Two years later, an “Indian Head” design was added to one side. The most recent design from the U.S. Mint was issued in 2010, featuring its “Union Shield” theme. It shows a shield on the tails side of the coin to represent “Lincoln’s preservation of the United States as a single country,” the U.S. Mint wrote.

images.caption: A pile of US one-cent coins, commonly known as pennies, is seen in Washington, DC, United States on Sept., 29, 2026.

articles.title: FBI investigating potential breach of its crime database
articles.summary: The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its National Crime Information Center, two people briefed on the matter told NBC News Friday.
articles.body: The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its National Crime Information Center, two people briefed on the matter told NBC News Friday. The FBI’s National Crime Information Center is used to connect federal, state and local authorities so that important law enforcement information is available nationwide. The FBI had no comment as of Friday night. CNN reported the matter earlier in the evening. While the FBI has not addressed who may have breached the system in this case, the agency did announce an investigation in September of a notorious hacking group that claimed it had stolen data on agents through the agency’s job portal. The breach this week follows an apparent cyberattack at the U.S. Department of Agriculture, as employees were informed Thursday that one of its systems had been targeted. USDA officials with knowledge of the matter said that a system the agency uses to pay farmers was hit by the breach, though as of Friday, no other systems were targeted. Officials raised alarms that the hackers could find a way to access more sensitive information due to the breach. Alongside the reported breaches, outages affecting both private and public sectors over the last several days have raised concerns about the nation’s cybersecurity. An internal classified computer network used by the National Security Agency endured a multi-day outage after it first went down Tuesday due to a technical problem, according to two people with knowledge of the matter. As of Friday, the outage has been resolved, sources said. Sources told NBC News that the network went down while maintenance was being performed. They said that there was no sign that the outage was caused by a cyberattack. Addressing the widespread tech outages, Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., the top Democrat on the Senate Intelligence Committee, said Wednesday that evidence showed that the tech outages were not caused by cyberattacks, though he warned that AI could have played a role in the systems’ vulnerabilities. Amid rising concerns about the outages, a White House official confirmed to NBC News Thursday that White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was leaving his role. Cairncross was directly involved with the White House’s deliberations on AI policy, including its move to direct Anthropic to take down its two most powerful AI systems over the summer due to national security concerns.

images.caption: Historical versions of the U.S. flag fly over the entrance to the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) headquarters building on September 15, 2024, in Washington, D.C.

articles.title: Rajasthan Congress chief Dotasra demands CM  resign over panchayat poll setback
articles.summary: Rajasthan PCC chief Govind Dotasra urges CM Bhajan Lal Sharma and cabinet to resign after BJP panchayat poll setback, citing public anger and governance failures.
articles.body: JAIPUR: Rajasthan Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) president Govind Singh Dotasra Friday demanded the resignation of chief minister Bhajan Lal Sharma and his cabinet, terming BJP’s setback in panchayat elections as “public anger” over alleged corruption, administrative lapses and unfulfilled promises.Addressing a news conference at the Congress office in Jaipur, Dotasra said the state govt was focused on optics rather than governance. “The state govt appears more interested in publicity and ceremonial events than addressing people’s problems,” he said.Taking aim at Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s earlier description of BJP’s urban local body performance as a “landslide victory,” Dotasra argued the results did not support the claim. He said BJP’s lead over Congress was marginal and claimed that “nearly 64% of voters voted against it” in the urban polls.“People have exposed the PM’s claim (in rural polls). Modi should be wary of the ‘facts’ fed to him by Rajasthan BJP, which only ends up embarrassing him,” Dotasra said.He reiterated his demand for resignations, saying, “If the CM and his ministers have even a little moral responsibility left, they should resign and tell the PM and the Union home minister that they have failed to meet the expectations of Rajasthan’s people.”Dotasra alleged the Sharma govt failed to address inflation, healthcare, fertiliser and seed availability for farmers, employment and women’s safety. Referring to alleged irregularities in medicines and medical equipment supplied to pregnant women, he accused the govt of evading accountability for maternal deaths. He also alleged that job seekers were facing police action. Unemployed youth, he said, were being met with “batons and police action instead of recruitment opportunities.”Dotasra also criticised Sharma over remarks directed at former chief minister Ashok Gehlot, saying Gehlot’s advice to keep relatives away from govt affairs stemmed from his experience as a three-term CM. “Instead of addressing the issue, the current CM appears rattled. The language he used against a former CM was unacceptable. Even a street drunkard would not use such language,” Dotasra said.Questioning Sharma’s emphasis on high-profile visits and public events, Dotasra took a swipe at the ceremonial aspects of VIP tours. “A ‘Radhe Radhe’ stole, a memento, a helicopter ride and visits by the PM and the Union HM—but what did Rajasthan’s people get? articles.title: Lawmakers warn Americans of vulnerable systems amid streak of outages: 'Something is going on'
articles.summary: Lawmakers warn America's power grids, water systems and banks are soft targets after a 10-day wave of tech outages raised cybersecurity concerns.
articles.body: Lawmakers are sounding the alarm over security threats in America's critical infrastructure following a 10-day wave of tech outages across major industries, warning about cybersecurity and the resilience of the nation's increasingly interconnected, vulnerable systems. "I will tell you from my dealing back in the intelligence world in the Pentagon, this is not normal," Rep. Keith Self, R-Texas, said. "Ask the questions." "Cybersecurity is a serious issue, and threats are becoming more serious," Sen. Jon Ossoff, D-Ga., said. TIMELINE: AMERICA HITS A TECH WALL AS OUTAGES CRIPPLE EMAIL, GROUND FLIGHTS AND DISRUPT MAJOR BANKS "These systems are complex," Rep. Pete Ricketts, R-Neb., said. "I used to run a company that had technology. It's not unusual." The lawmakers' concerns come as the nation continues to experience tech outages, including at the National Security Agency, and grapples with whether the recent disruptions were isolated technical failures or signs of a broader cybersecurity threat. President Donald Trump's administration says the incidents were unrelated and were not caused by malicious actors. But speculation continues to increase, particularly after Trump fired National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross on Thursday over concerns that he lacked the proper credentials in cybersecurity for the job. "The question has got to be asked, ‘Is there an offensive cyberattack going on that we're not going to hear about?’" Self said. "Because I don't believe any of the public statements that are made, because something is going on behind the scenes." RECENT SERVICE OUTAGES NOT STATE-SPONSORED ATTACKS, DNI JAY CLAYTON TESTIFIES Officials say that as artificial intelligence gets better at spotting holes in a system's security, those systems are coming under more strain as companies try to patch those holes. Regardless of what caused the disruptions, lawmakers warned that the incidents underscore a broader concern: America's reliance on interconnected technology has created potential vulnerabilities across critical infrastructure, from local water systems and power grids to banking and aviation. "The localized municipal-based infrastructure in America is a soft target," Sen. Tim Sheehy, R-Mont., told Fox News Digital. "And that's been flagged for decades. We haven't addressed it fully. And I think over the past week, we've seen it's time we get serious about it." $1M-A-DAY CHINA TECH CRACKDOWN PROPOSED AMID CASCADE OF US CYBER DISRUPTIONS "Everything's interconnected now, so we've got to be working on security all the time," Sen. John Hoeven, R-N.D., said. "Cybersecurity is a big deal, and it's not just in government, but in business as well, and that's what we're seeing. There's been a number of these incidents around the country now and, obviously, people are concerned about it and we should be." Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., encouraged keeping conversation around cyber threats and developing U.S. systems to reduce vulnerability as a bipartisan issue. articles.title: Iran says it downed US drones over Hormuz as bid to end war remains stalled
articles.summary: Iran reiterates conditions for Hormuz reopening as US slaps sanctions on four Iranians it says acted as ‘oil trustees’.
articles.body:
Iranian forces say they have shot down two US drones over the Strait of Hormuz, as the United States steps up its economic pressure campaign against Iran.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Saturday a new air defence system had intercepted and shot down an MQ-9 drone, according to Iranian state broadcaster IRIB. It said the incident marked the 58th such drone brought down by Iranian forces since the start of the war nearly nine months ago.

Later on Saturday, the IRGC also claimed bringing down an MQ-1 drone over Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, the 19th such downing.

There was no immediate comment by the US military.

The incidents come days after the US and Iran engaged in direct, tit-for-tat strikes , against a backdrop of increasing Iranian attacks on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz, the vital waterway through which one-fifth of the world’s oil and gas passed in peacetime.

Launched by the US and Israel on February 28, the war has killed thousands of people and severely disrupted shipping, pushing global energy prices higher and spreading to countries across the region.

The US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding in June, but it was never fully implemented because of disagreements over freedom and security of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, with attacks resuming periodically since July. In August, The Washington Post reported that the US had lost 45 MQ-9 drones, or about 25 percent of its fleet at a cost of more than $1.3bn, during combat operations in Iran.

As an agreement to end the war remains elusive, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Friday outlined his country’s positions on negotiations with the US, citing a seven-day proposal delivered to the US in September.

In an interview with state media, Araghchi said the seven conditions Iran has put forward “must be implemented for the Strait of Hormuz to reopen”. The conditions include ending the war and lifting sanctions and the naval blockade on Iran’s southern ports.

Araghchi said Iran was prepared to negotiate how the conditions should be implemented, saying its timetable was “flexible”. The negotiations would be “conditional on the American side taking necessary confidence-building measures”, he added.

The top diplomat also ruled out Iran transferring its stockpile of 60 percent enriched uranium abroad, but said a “fair solution” could be reached and a number of proposals by mediators were “worth examining”.

Araghchi said that the current “no war, no peace” state of the conflict was undesirable, but that Iran could not accept an agreement that would “hand victory to the other side”.

At a Friday news conference at the White House, US President Donald Trump told reporters that Tehran “want to make a deal” but not one that is acceptable to him.

“We want to make a real deal, not a fake deal that they’ve been doing for 51 years,” alleged Trump, who had said last week that a deal with Iran on ending the war was unnecessary.

At the same news conference, US Vice President JD Vance, who had previously blamed the war for Republicans losing both chambers of Congress earlier this month, declined to say whether he would have authorised strikes on Iran to prevent the country from developing a nuclear weapon.

Vance said the decision to attack Iran in February was Trump’s call, “and my job is to support the president of the United States.”

The Treasury said in a statement that ⁠⁠in many cases the trustees have kept oil revenues for personal gain. Among the individuals sanctioned are Mohammad Javad Bavand, a former IRGC intelligence officer, and Majid Taj, brother of ‌‌the Iranian Football Federation’s President Mehdi Taj, the Treasury said.

The new sanctions put ⁠⁠the individuals on the Treasury Office of Foreign Assets Control’s Specially Designated Nationals list, freezing any assets they may have under US jurisdiction and effectively prohibiting dollar ⁠⁠transactions with them or entities that they control.

The Treasury also said it imposed sanctions ⁠⁠on Mohammad Hossein Servati, the son of IRGC ⁠⁠Brigadier General Mohsen Servati, who has held positions in companies that brokered and received shipments of Iranian oil for delivery to independent Chinese “teapot” refineries.

Another sanctioned individual is ‌‌Mojtaba Arabnejad, the son of the sanctioned Mahan Air CEO Hamid Arabnejad. The Treasury said that Mojtaba Arabnejad has purchased aircraft ‌‌parts ‌‌for the sanctioned Mahan Air and overseen oil sales that have partly supported the airline.

Meanwhile, as Republicans grapple with the fallout from the sweeping midterm election losses, Democratic Representatives Yassamin Ansari and Ro Khanna called on Congress to use an upcoming government funding bill to end spending for offensive military operations against Iran.

Citing the mounting costs of the war, they issued a video statement urging fellow legislators to reject any funding package that keeps paying for the war, with a deadline looming next month to adopt a budget.

Failing to pass a spending bill by December 11 could trigger a government shutdown, a risk that has made some Democrats wary of drawing a red line on the war on Iran.

Rosa DeLauro and Patty Murray, the top Democrats responsible for appropriations, have said they would prefer to find ways to end the war without risking a government shutdown.

articles.title: 2028 presidential contender under fire from state auditor over waste, fraud, abuse fears: 'Troubling response'
articles.summary: Kentucky's top auditor says $1.5 billion in taxpayer waste was uncovered, accusing Democratic Gov. Andy Beshear of brushing off Medicaid and SNAP findings.
articles.body: Kentucky’s top auditor says her office has uncovered $1.5 billion in taxpayer waste across state government and accused Democratic Gov. Andy Beshear, widely believed to have presidential aspirations, of brushing off the findings instead of helping fix them. "I wish I could say that I had more support and help from the governor's office in Kentucky, but I haven't really and that's one of the reasons why I'm very public with our reports. I'm very public with our findings, because I need the public's help," Ball said in an interview this week at a State Financial Officers Foundation (SFOF) conference in Philadelphia. "I need the backlash that comes when you see money just being flushed down the toilet, when you see that you're losing money, especially in Medicaid. It's money that should go to people who are actually in need, and we're losing those dollars." Over the past year, Ball’s office flagged $836 million in wasteful Medicaid spending that was primarily driven by multi-state concurrent enrollment, where Kentucky continued paying monthly managed care capitation fees for individuals simultaneously enrolled in Medicaid in up to eight other states. TRUMP ADMIN PAUSING OVER $1B IN MEDICAID PAYMENTS TO MINNESOTA, CALIFORNIA OVER FRAUD, COMPLIANCE CONCERNS Her audits also flagged ineligible noncitizens receiving benefits, single Social Security numbers being used by up to 10 people at once, duplicate individual payments, and roughly $100 million in SNAP benefit errors, bringing the total waste she cited across state benefit programs to $1.5 billion. "I have had conversations with the governor's staff," Ball explained. "We are always letting the governor know, 'Hey, this is what we found.' We also offer solutions all the time. And typically what I get back is, like for the $836 million of Medicaid dollars that we found, is that, 'Well, that happens everywhere. You know, that's not unique to us.' And that's really a troubling response. If your attitude is like, 'Well, it's not just us, you know, we're not really doing a horrible job because it happens other places too,' that explains why problems like this continue." RNC RIPS BESHEAR'S 'WOKE TRANS RECORD' OVER VETO OF KENTUCKY GIRLS' SPORTS BILL Additionally, Ball’s office released a report earlier this year outlining spending by Beshear’s executive branch in fiscal year 2025 that, while not illegal, flagged what she called "massive" issues of extravagant spending of tax dollars that "needs to stop." The "concerning expenditures" listed include $183,576 in out-of-state travel costs, including $7,632 for a limousine in Germany; a $17,013 dinner at a Kentucky distillery; and $360,000 for 75 people to attend a two-day conference within the Commonwealth. "I think one thing that I have realized is that the governor doesn't like bad news. And unfortunately, a lot of times when I come in, and I do an audit, the news that I have is bad," Ball said. "But what I also try to remind people, it's good too, in the sense that I also have a recommendation for how to fix it. So, while it is important to identify the problems — and I do that — I'm also hyper-focused on the solution. And I would encourage the governor to jump in and help me be part of the solution to this. That's not been the experience that I've had. I've not had cooperation, and I would love to have that. I think that that's what Kentuckians deserve." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Beshear’s office has repeatedly pushed back on Ball’s criticisms, dismissing her $836 million Medicaid waste estimate as "a wild extrapolation from a small subset" and maintaining that once Kentucky gained access to updated federal cross-check databases, actual multi-state overlap numbers were "nothing remotely close to that." In a statement to Fox News Digital, his office said the governor has "created a fiscally responsible administration, securing six consecutive budget surpluses, the five best years on record for economic investment and upgrades from all three major bond rating agencies while also cutting income and property taxes. His management of the state is delivering positive results, so hardworking Kentuckians can live better lives." Beshear's office added that Ball's report has "significant errors and inaccuracies" and suggested she focus on "real threats looming in Kentucky due to Trump's ‘Big, Ugly Bill,’ which risks the closure of 35 rural hospitals, the jobs of 20,000 healthcare workers and health coverage for thousands of Kentuckians." When it comes to potential Medicaid waste, fraud and abuse, Ball told Fox News Digital it is unlikely that money can be clawed back, heightening the importance of stopping it before it begins. The Trump administration has made cracking down on fraud this year and set up the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud in March which has reported that federal agencies have identified $260.7 billion in estimated fraud since January 2025. Ball told Fox News Digital that heading into 2027, she sees a "tremendous opportunity" to address waste, fraud, and abuse in Kentucky because the "public cares right now, I think, at a level that they've not cared before." "I've always cared about protecting taxpayer dollars, I've also cared about stopping waste, fraud, and abuse. I care about complying with the law," Ball said. "I think this is this beautiful moment right now where the public deeply cares about it too. So I think I have an opportunity. I think other auditors around the country, other people who are in similar roles, have opportunities like it's never been before where we really can take the effort to stop these things from happening."6408662620112

articles.title: Republicans face 'brutal' 2028 Senate map after Dems 2026 blue wave
articles.summary: Incoming NRSC chair Sen. Bernie Moreno calls the GOP's 2028 Senate map "absolutely brutal" as Republicans must flip six seats to reclaim majority control.
articles.body: Incoming Senate Republican campaign chairman says the party faces a "very tough" road ahead as the GOP aims to take back their majority in 2028 after taking significant losses in the midterms earlier this month. Democrats convincingly grabbed control of the Senate and will hold a large 56-44 majority when the new Congress is sworn in at the start of the new year, they also won control of the House and multiple governors' seats flip from red to blue, as well. In the Senate, the new split means Republicans will need to flip at least six seats in the 2028 elections to win back the majority. That number rises to seven seats if they lose the White House in the next election cycle. One senator told Fox News Digital that Republicans can "forget 2028." "It is an absolutely brutal map," Ohio Sen. Bernie Moreno, the incoming National Republican Senatorial Committee chair, recently told Fox News Digital, as he pointed to the states up for grabs in 2028. SENATE REPUBLICANS FEAR 'BRUTAL' 2028 MAP COULD KEEP DEMOCRATS IN POWER FOR YEARS But the first term senator from Ohio added that in "politics, things change pretty quickly." He's not kidding. At the start of the 2026 cycle, the Democrats faced a steep and narrow path to winning back the majority, but by Election Day the party was able to ride a massive blue wave formed by an extremely favorable political climate to flip nine Senate seats . Senate Majority Leader John Thune, looking ahead to the next election, said in an interview on Fox News' "America Reports, "We can come back — we will." "I've been there before, and we just have to get out and win the hearts and minds of the American people," he added. "And that means coming up with a compelling economic message, talking about secure streets, secure border, safe streets, and in more money in your pocket. I mean, I think those are the things that the American people care the most about." Looking ahead to the next two years, when he will be leading the GOP minority in the Senate, Thune said "we now have an opportunity in the minority to draw those bold lines, those contrasts, and make sure that we are delivering a message that connects with the middle of the electorate." In 2028, Republicans will need to hold onto seats in battlegrounds Wisconsin and North Carolina, where GOP Sens. Ron Johnson and Ted Budd are up for re-election. Meanwhile, Republicans will work to flip seats held by Democratic Sens. Mark Kelly of Arizona, John Fetterman of Pennsylvania, Raphael Warnock of Georgia, Catherine Cortez Masto of Nevada, and Maggie Hassan of New Hampshire. Dem flips key Senate seat in battleground North Carolina as Cooper defeats Trump ally TRUMP GRIP ON GOP FACES MAJOR POST-ELECTION TEST Fetterman, who has repeatedly visibly broken with his party and seen his poll numbers among Democrats crater, faces all-but-certain primary challenges if he seeks re-election. Meanwhile, Kelly and Warnock are mulling White House runs in 2028. Senate showdowns will also be held in 2028 in six states that President Donald Trump carried by double-digits two years ago that become key battlegrounds in this year's midterms. Among them are Ohio, where former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown won a ticket back to the Senate with a five point victory over appointed GOP Sen. Jon Husted. Brown will fill out the final two years of Vice President JD Vance's old Senate term, so he'll face re-election in 2028. Republicans will be defending seats in four states where Democrats scored Senate flips in this year's midterms. The four seats are held by GOP Sens. Chuck Grassley of Iowa, Jerry Moran of Kansas, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, and Tim Scott of South Carolina, Massive upset: Andrews downs Trump-backed Graham in ruby-red South Carolina In Florida, appointed Republican Sen. Ashley Moody narrowly defeated progressive Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon in a special election. Moody, who is filling out Secretary of State Marco Rubio's old Senate term, will face re-election in two years. SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER Kyle Kondik, managing editor of Sabato’s Crystal Ball at the University of Virginia Center for Politics, which is a leading nonpartisan political handicapper, told Fox News Digital Republicans could win the Senate back by flipping six states in 2028 : Arizona, Georgia, Ohio, Nevada, New Hampshire, and Pennsylvania. Dems seize the Senate as blue tidal wave crashes deep into Trump country, topples GOP strongholds "Those are five states Trump won state in 2024," as well as New Hampshire, which then-Vice President Kamala Harris carried by single digits. "The Democrats just showed that they could win all these double-digit Trump states" in the midterms," Kondik noted. "The Republicans don't have to flip any double-digit Harris states to win the Senate back" in 2028. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Kondik also highlighted that there there will be a Senate special election next November, a year ahead of the 2028 showdowns. That ballot box contest will be held in Minnesota, where Democratic Sen. Amy Klobuchar is about to step down after winning the state's gubernatorial election. Klobuchar will pick a replacement senator when she steps down, and the state will hold a special contest on Election Day 2027 to choose a successor to fill out the final three years of Klobuchar's current term.
